sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Freeze the candidate: deterministic validation is valid, all declared ship-owned operands and results have required quantity/unit cardinality, constants use exact inclusive bounds, the dimensionless clamp uses the canonical UNITLESS unit, and both readiness formulas include the required operands, inclusive clamp, registered trigonometric IRIs, degree/radian conversion, singular-input rejection, and expected-result-scaled tolerance.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: The candidate is only a presence/unit envelope and omits both semanticObligations. Add readiness constraints or an explicitly represented calculation/evidence structure covering psi = atan(tan(phi2)/sin(alpha)) with the registered math:sin, math:tan, and math:atan IRIs, degree/radian conversion, singular-input rejection, and tolerance comparison; do not use bare trigonometric syntax. Encode C3=845, C4=42, C5=825, all Table 3-2 f/g constants, and the inclusive clamp [5,20] rather than merely requiring their quantities. The derived psi and clamped term must not use exact equality; use tolerance scaled from the expected result. Also remove guessed xsd:decimal constraints because canonical datatype metadata is null, or supply an authoritative declared datatype.

Preserve the prior repair requirements: this remains only a presence/unit envelope and is not freezeable. Under COMPLEX_READINESS, add a faithful readiness structure for both declared results, including the psi relation psi = atan(tan(phi2)/sin(alpha)) using the registered math:sin, math:tan, and math:atan IRIs, explicit degree/radian conversion, singular-input rejection, and a tolerance comparison scaled from the expected derived psi rather than exact equality. Add the calculation/readiness linkage for the declared operands and results, and represent the clamped term as ((L*T)/B^2)^3 with L=shipLength, T=iceClassDraught, B=shipBreadth, followed by the inclusive [5,20] clamp; a bare result presence/range is insufficient. Retain exact inclusive bounds for C3=845, C4=42, C5=825 and all Table 3-2 f/g constants, with their supplied units. Remove the guessed xsd:decimal numeric-bound constraints unless an authoritative datatype is supplied. Do not use bare trigonometric functions or exact equality for derived results; no vocabulary matcher is needed because all required canonical terms are already supplied.

Do not freeze this candidate. Preserve the prior semantic repairs, but fix two remaining pass/unit defects: use the canonical dimensionless unit http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/UNITLESS for clampedHullGeometryTerm instead of kilogramPerSquareMetreSquareSecondUnit; and require exactly one qudt:numericValue (sh:minCount 1 and sh:maxCount 1) on every required QuantityValue, including all operands, constants, and both derived results. Without numericValue cardinality, missing values can satisfy the nested unit shapes and cause both SPARQL constraints to find no violation, while the constant bounds are also vacuous. Retain the registered math:sin/math:tan/math:atan IRIs, degree/radian conversion, singular-input rejection, tolerance scaled from each expected derived result, exact inclusive bounds for the constants, and the inclusive [5,20] clamp. No vocabulary matcher is needed.

Freeze the candidate: deterministic validation is valid, all declared ship-owned operands and results have required quantity/unit cardinality, constants use exact inclusive bounds, the dimensionless clamp uses the canonical UNITLESS unit, and both readiness formulas include the required operands, inclusive clamp, registered trigonometric IRIs, degree/radian conversion, singular-input rejection, and expected-result-scaled tolerance.
